utterances.text: Mr. Gagic, would you be willing to provide the original for inspection to the parties and to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can do that immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the usher could then receive it from -- and from the witness and give it to the Registrar so that it's available for inspection by the parties. Yes, that might take some time to look through it, but it's -- it's not lost. So, therefore, please proceed, Mr. Bakrac, meanwhile.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagic, from April 1992 when you returned to Belgrade onwards, can you just briefly tell us what duties did you discharge?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After my return to Belgrade, I worked until 1996 as head of the section for prevention of violent crime at the Belgrade SUP. In 1996, I was assigned to the chief of the section for preventing violent crimes at the seat of the ministry. That is to say, the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, where I remained until 2004. In 2004, I was appointed chief of the service for investigation of war crimes in the MUP of Serbia. I stayed there until 2006, when I retired.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagic, in the period between 2004 and 2006, did you do any operative work that had to do with the arrest of the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, the summary of the expected testimony tells the Chamber that whilst the witness was in charge of the war crimes department, proceedings were lodged against members of the Skorpioni and Zuti. And I wonder to what extent there is any dispute about proceedings instituted against members of those organisations. Unless, of course, there would be certain details which you would like to present. But, Ms. Friedman, is there any dispute about such proceedings being instituted against member of the Skorpions and the Wasps?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: There's no dispute about proceedings being instituted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: In addition, the witness appears to have some papers in front of him. Could we inquire what they are?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Or to be put away. Witness, you apparently have some papers in front of you. Could you tell us what they are.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have here in front of me the information about persons from these two groups who were arrested. These were the Skorpions and the Yellow Wasps. And I have it as an aide-memoire, and I can remove it, if needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would please remove it, and if you want to consult it, then please tell us. Mr. Bakrac, the fact that proceedings were instituted against these members of those units is not in dispute. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will spend a very short time on this, maybe three or four questions, because it is not so important. Just the basics.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you were involved in the arrest of Yellow Wasps, did you learn whether they had any connections with the MUP of the Republic of Serbia? At the time of the commission of these crimes or later on, did they have any connections, any links, with the MUP or the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the information that I am aware of seems to suggest that members of the Yellow Wasps never had anything to do with either the members of the MUP or with members of the State Security Department. If they had individual contacts, then it's something that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you become aware in the course of your operative work that one of the accused and prosecuted, Branko Popovic, who was also known as Major Marko Pavlovic, in Zvornik, in 1992, had any links or connections whatsoever with the MUP or the DB of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any links he would have with either the MUP or the DB of the Republic of Serbia, nor was such a link established during investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You also participated -- oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that my learned friend is on her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I just wanted to seek some clarification. I know Mr. Bakrac has shortened his questions. But I don't think it's clear on the record exactly which investigations this witness oversaw or was involved in. Maybe we should get back to that for a little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, that proceedings were instituted is agreed, but what investigation the witness is talking about seems to be not clear at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in what way did you participate in the investigation that had to do with the arrests of the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I arrested the members of the Yellow Wasps after I received a request from the prosecutor for war crimes to do that. And, as far as I know, the war crimes prosecutor of the Republic of Serbia received the necessary information from ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you reviewed the files, did you have any interviews with the arrested persons?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after an arrest, the principle is to interview each individual in order to establish his identity, his possible involvement in the relevant incident, then a report is drawn up which includes all the relevant information, and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I get the impression that you would like to answer the question with yes. The question was: Did you interview persons arrested. Did you? Then the answer is yes. If not, then the answer is no. Please proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did any of the persons say in these interviews that they were members of the MUP or the DB of the Republic of Serbia at any point?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As for the documents and files which you received from the prosecutor's office, did any of that suggest that there were links between any of them and the MUP or the DB of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gagic. In order to shorten --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, I see that my learned friend is already on her feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted to seek some clarification because the documents that we have are about investigations in around 1993. And the witness is apparently referring to proceedings that happened when he was in charge in 2004 or so. So if there some documentation of the later proceedings, then we could know exactly which individuals we're talking about and which incidents, in order to know what his investigation could or could not have revealed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, you could clarify that in cross-examination, Ms. Friedman. But, Mr. Bakrac, you know already that it's a matter which is of some interest to Ms. Friedman. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to finish in the next few minutes, and then I will, with your leave, allow my learned friend Ms. Friedman to clarify that. And I allow that there have been differences between arrests and some procedures between those that were conducted in 1993 and 2004. So let me ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: As for the Skorpions, I suppose that, once again, you had files and you conducted interviews?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Well, let me try to help my learned friend Ms. Friedman. As for the Skorpions, what crime did this have to do with; and at what time was the crime committed?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the crime which occurred in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina on Mount Treskavica, and it occurred in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: During your operative work, that is to say, taking statements and receiving files from the prosecutor's office, did you establish any sort of link between this group, i.e., the Skorpions, and the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia or the State Security Department of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagic, before I thank the Bench for the time allotted, let me just ask you something that I may have omitted. You mentioned a member of the Novi Sad Corps Ivanovic, who used to come to the training centre of the TO in Erdut. Can you tell us whether you know his first name and whether you know the position he held in the Novi Sad Corps?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His first name is Bora. Possibly Borislav, though I think it is just Bora, and I think that he was the Chief of Staff in the command of the Novi Sad Corps, which means that he was, by virtue of that position, also the deputy of Major Biorcevic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: General Biorcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Your Honours, if you would allow me just an additional two minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two minutes. Please use them ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mr. Gagic, do you know whether the Skorpions were engaged in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know how they were engaged; and how did they arrive in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sent to Kosovo as the reserve forces, the reservist part of the special anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Of what MUP?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did they have this status previously or did they get that status at that time; and, if so, in what way?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They received that status immediately before their entry into Kosovo. They even waited for about 20 days for their status to be determined. And they reserved such a status at the proposal of Vlastimir Djordjevic. The reason for that was that the commander of the SAJ, Zivko Trajkovic, insisted that their status had to be determined and that they -- he did not wish the presence of any paramilitaries in the zone where he was conducting operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And if I understood you correctly, after that, they got a status within the public security service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: GVOZDEN GAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. These were the two minutes that I asked for. Thanks a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gagic. These were all the questions I had for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bakrac. One matter. Document 2D1056, which is the military booklet, has not been assigned a number yet. Madam Registrar, in order to have it marked for identification it receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number will be for 2D1056, D694, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D694 is marked for identification. The original is in the hands of Madam Registrar at this moment, available for inspections by the parties. Then I would like to briefly spend some time on scheduling issues. It was confirmed to me that we could sit next week, Monday, that is, the 13th of February, in the afternoon, quarter past 2.00 until 7.00. That we could sit on Tuesday, the 14th, also in the afternoon, quarter past 2.00. And then we would sit on Wednesday, 9.00 -- from 9.00 to a quarter to 2.00. As far as witnesses are concerned, how much time would you need for Witness DFS-011?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Two hours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two hours. Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Three and a half, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would bring us well into Tuesday already. Would the next witness, which will be a Stanisic witness, be ready on from Tuesday or Wednesday next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. All the formalities have been completed --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We're expecting -- Your Honour, yes. We're expecting him to arrive on Sunday, we're expecting to proof him on Monday, ready to begin on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bakrac, gives this sufficient guidance for the witnesses who come after that, because they certainly will not be -- how much time would you need with your witness, Mr. Jordash, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: An afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: An afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So three hours, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that the witnesses coming after that, Mr. Bakrac, will certainly not start the testimony next week. We'll first have to see whether we can finish the testimony of the witness, which is unlikely to happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes. And we're still waiting for an estimate, I think, from the Prosecution, so -- on that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But I think Mr. Bakrac now has sufficient guidance as not to bring in witnesses too early, and we know what to expect. Then we'd like to see you back on Monday afternoon, Mr. Gagic. We'll start then at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon. I again instruct you that you should not speak to anyone about your testimony, whether the testimony you have given yesterday and today, or whether that is the testimony still to be given next week. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may follow the usher. And I'll see whether on my list of procedural matters there's anything that could not wait until Monday. The witness may be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's one brief matter, Mr. Jordash, I'd like to raise, which is about Witness Pelevic. You have objected during the examination of that witness that the Prosecution had violated Rule 90(H)(ii). On the 31st of January, you stated, when asked, that you did not seek an immediate ruling on your objections but would make further motions on the matter at a later time. The parties were instructed to at least discuss the matters among themselves. Chamber staff received a copy of an e-mail asking some questions from the Prosecution. Is there any update to be reported at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'd like to hear from you as soon as possible, because we have to, sooner or later, find out whether your objections still stand or not. Well, the objections may stand, but what remedy you are seeking.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well -- yes, we'll discuss it further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And if you seek a remedy, it's about what questions exactly that were put to that witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes? Then we adjourn, and we will resume on Monday, the 13th of February, a quarter past 2.00 in this same courtroom, II.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
